cards.front_question: What classical geometric tools are permitted for pure geometric constructions?
cards.back_answer: Only an unmarked straightedge (ruler) for drawing straight lines and a compass for drawing circular arcs and measuring distances.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 1

cards.front_question: Describe the construction steps and equidistance property of a perpendicular bisector of segment XY.
cards.back_answer: Draw intersecting arcs above and below XY from endpoints X and Y using compass radius > 0.5 XY. The line joining arc intersections bisects XY at 90°. Equidistance property: Any point on the perpendicular bisector is at equal distance from X and Y.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 2

cards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: How is a 60° angle c...]
cards.front_question: How is a 60° angle constructed using ruler and compass, and why does this method work?
cards.back_answer: Draw an arc from vertex A intersecting a ray at B. Without changing compass radius, draw an arc from B intersecting the first arc at C. Ray AC forms a 60° angle because ΔABC has three equal sides (radius), making it an equilateral triangle.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 3

cards.front_question: How can 30°, 15°, and 45° angles be derived systematically from primary constructions?
cards.back_answer: 30° is constructed by bisecting a 60° angle; 15° is constructed by bisecting a 30° angle; 45° is constructed by bisecting a 90° right angle.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 4

cards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: Why is a regular hex...]
cards.front_question: Why is a regular hexagon composed of 6 equilateral triangles at its center, and what is its interior angle measure?
cards.back_answer: Stepping off the circle radius 6 times along its circumference produces 6 congruent equilateral triangles meeting at the center (6 × 60° = 360°). Each interior angle of the regular hexagon equals 2 × 60° = 120°.
cards.graphic_description: Visual diagram representing key concept for card 5

cards.front_question: What is Tiling (Tessellation) and what are the 7 pieces of a traditional Tangram puzzle?
cards.back_answer: Tiling is covering a 2D plane with geometric shapes with zero gaps and zero overlaps. A Tangram consists of 7 pieces: 5 triangles (2 large, 1 medium, 2 small), 1 square, and 1 parallelogram.
